validated_results.title: Serum alpha-tocopherol and gamma-tocopherol in relation to prostate cancer risk in a prospective study.
validated_results.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
validated_results.reason: Nested case-control study within the ATBC cohort reporting serum alpha-tocopherol (vitamin E) concentrations in relation to incident prostate cancer risk.

extraction.comparison_type: highest versus lowest tertile of serum alpha-tocopherol
extraction.population: Finnish men aged 50-69 years in the ATBC Study cohort

sample_size.excerpt: From the ATBC Study cohort of 29 133 Finnish men, 50-69 years old, we randomly selected 100 incident prostate cancer case patients and matched 200 control subjects.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 100 + 200 = 300

cases.excerpt: From the ATBC Study cohort of 29 133 Finnish men, 50-69 years old, we randomly selected 100 incident prostate cancer case patients and matched 200 control subjects.

effect_size.excerpt: Odds ratios for the highest versus the lowest tertiles were 0.49 (95% CI = 0.24 to 1.01, P(trend) = .05) for alpha-tocopherol and 0.57 (95% CI = 0.31 to 1.06, P(trend) = .08) for gamma-tocopherol. Further analyses indicated that the association of high serum tocopherols with low prostate cancer risk was stronger in the alpha-tocopherol-supplemented group than in those not receiving alpha-tocopherol.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Odds ratios for the highest versus the lowest tertiles were 0.49 (95% CI = 0.24 to 1.01, P(trend) = .05) for alpha-tocopherol and 0.57 (95% CI = 0.31 to 1.06, P(trend) = .08) for gamma-tocopherol.

validated_results.title: Risk of prostate cancer in a randomized clinical trial of calcium supplementation.
validated_results.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
validated_results.reason: Randomized placebo-controlled trial of calcium carbonate supplementation reporting prostate cancer incidence rate ratios.

extraction.timing: pre-diagnosis supplementation with mean follow-up of 10.3 years
extraction.population: 672 men randomized in a colorectal adenoma chemoprevention trial

sample_size.excerpt: We randomly assigned 672 men to receive either 3 g of calcium carbonate (1,200 mg of calcium), or placebo, daily for 4 years in a colorectal adenoma chemoprevention trial. Participants were followed for up to 12 years and asked periodically to report new cancer diagnoses.

cases.excerpt: After a mean follow-up of 10.3 years, there were 33 prostate cancer cases in the calcium-treated group and 37 in the placebo-treated group [unadjusted rate ratio, 0.83; 95% confidence interval (95% CI), 0.52-1.32].
cases.location: abstract, results; cases derived from reported group counts 33 + 37 = 70

effect_size.excerpt: We used life table and Cox proportional hazard models to compute rate ratios for prostate cancer incidence and generalized linear models to assess the relative risk of increases in PSA levels. After a mean follow-up of 10.3 years, there were 33 prostate cancer cases in the calcium-treated group and 37 in the placebo-treated group [unadjusted rate ratio, 0.83; 95% confidence interval (95% CI), 0.52-1.32].
